description: Six locales stress-testing the Svelte 5 data grid: en, de, fr-CA, ja, ar and he. Switching a chip translates headers, buttons and status pills, flips document direction for Arabic and Hebrew, and drives number, currency and date formatting through Intl with Arabic-Indic digits, narrow non-breaking spaces in fr-CA, era in ja-JP and CLDR currency placement. It checks the procurement list: headers right-align with the sort indicator on the left in RTL, pinned columns pin to the correct edge, filter menus anchor correctly, numbers stay tabular and mixed-direction text is isolated with bdi.

faq.question: How does the grid handle RTL?
faq.answer: It reads the direction of its container. With dir='rtl' the header alignment, sort indicator position, pinned edges and menu anchors mirror, without any RTL-specific props.

faq.question: How is mixed-direction text kept readable?
faq.answer: Cells that combine a Latin brand name with Arabic text wrap the embedded run in bidi isolation, so the digits and brand stay in reading order inside the RTL sentence.

faq.question: Where do the formats come from?
faq.answer: From Intl.NumberFormat and Intl.DateTimeFormat with the active locale, which is why fr-CA gets narrow non-breaking spaces and ar-SA gets the full Arabic month name with no custom code.
